command: cd ui && npm run test:run -- multiWindow
summary: 31 tests pass; all seven per-window isolation properties verified for two-and-three-window scenarios.

isolationProperties.name: Destination isolation
isolationProperties.description: Tab change in Window A (Overview→Recall) does not affect Window B's state, revision, generation, or AbortSignal.

isolationProperties.name: Query isolation
isolationProperties.description: Search (beginRequest, completeRequest, failRequest) in Window A with query 'foo' does not change Window B's query state, revision, or session state (Window B holds query 'bar').

isolationProperties.name: Policy isolation
isolationProperties.description: Policy hash from Window A does not invalidate entries in Window B's independent SnapshotCache; patchReducer rejects cross-policy patches; guardPolicy rejects the foreign hash.

isolationProperties.name: Selection isolation
isolationProperties.description: Selecting entity X in Window A leaves Window B's selected entity Y items and session state unchanged in the reducer.

isolationProperties.name: Camera isolation
isolationProperties.description: Camera zoom=2.0 pan=(100,200) mutation in Window A does not alter Window B's camera (zoom=1.0 pan=(0,0)); cache invalidation and AbortSignal cancellation remain per-window.

isolationProperties.name: Quality isolation
isolationProperties.description: Quality mode downgrade (full-scene→list-first) in Window A does not affect Window B's reducer items, reducer state reference, or SnapshotCache entries.

isolationProperties.name: Reducer ownership
isolationProperties.description: Each window has a separate MemoryWindowSessionV2 instance and ReducerState<T> value. All five PatchAction types (APPLY_PATCH, CONFIRM_WRITE, ROLLBACK_WRITE, INVALIDATE, REFETCH_REQUIRED) dispatched to Window A have zero effect on Window B's reducer.

integrationScenarios.name: Three windows with all distinct dimensions
integrationScenarios.description: Three windows (A: Overview/ph-A/entity-A, B: Recall/ph-B/memory-B, C: Knowledge/ph-C/evidence-C) operate simultaneously. All operations (session lifecycle, patch apply, markDetached, reset, cache invalidation) remain strictly per-window with zero cross-window mutation.

invariantsVerified: One window cannot reset or leak state into another
Each MemoryWindowSessionV2 instance owns its own generation counter, revision, AbortController, and lifecycle state
patchReducer is a pure function returning new state; separate calls with separate state values cannot cross-contaminate
SnapshotCache instances are independent; invalidateByPolicy and invalidateByRevision operate only on the calling instance's internal Map
guardPolicy rejects any foreign policyHash at the session level
patchReducer rejects patches with mismatched policy_hash, schemaVersion, or base_revision — cross-window patches are naturally rejected

command: cd ui && npm run test:run -- snapshotCacheReuse
summary: 25 tests pass; all seven exact key-matching properties (P-REUSE, P-REV, P-SCHEMA, P-POLICY, P-QUERY, P-ALL, P-PARTIAL) verified plus two-window integration scenarios.

cacheKeyProperties.name: Compatible cache reuse
cacheKeyProperties.description: Two windows with identical (schemaVersion, revision, policyHash, queryHash) hit the same cached snapshot.

cacheKeyProperties.name: Revision mismatch rejection
cacheKeyProperties.description: Cache miss when revision differs by even 1; also covers revision-1, revision+1, and large gap.

cacheKeyProperties.name: Schema mismatch rejection
cacheKeyProperties.description: Cache miss when schemaVersion differs (e.g. '2.0' vs '2.1', '1.0' vs '2.0', empty string vs '2.0').

cacheKeyProperties.name: Policy mismatch rejection
cacheKeyProperties.description: Cache miss when policyHash differs; prefix collisions do not occur.

cacheKeyProperties.name: All-fields-match hits
cacheKeyProperties.description: Cache hit only when ALL four key fields match exactly; four single-field variants are independent entries.

cacheKeyProperties.name: Partial match does not hit
cacheKeyProperties.description: 3 matching fields + 1 different field = cache miss; all four combinations (each field as the odd-one-out) verified.

integrationScenarios.name: Two windows — shared context hits, distinct context misses
integrationScenarios.description: Window A writes snapshot for (qh-search, rev10); Window B with same key gets the snapshot; Window B with different query or revision misses.

integrationScenarios.name: Stale revision guard
integrationScenarios.description: A revision-9 entry written by Window A is never served to a revision-10 reader.

integrationScenarios.name: Policy-namespaced independent snapshots
integrationScenarios.description: Window A (ph-a) and Window B (ph-b) sharing the same cache instance store independent policy-namespaced snapshots; no cross-policy bleed.

invariantsVerified: Cache reuse requires exact match on all four fields: schemaVersion, revision, policyHash, queryHash
A difference of 1 in revision is sufficient to produce a cache miss
A different schemaVersion string is sufficient to produce a cache miss
A different policyHash string is sufficient to produce a cache miss
A different queryHash string is sufficient to produce a cache miss
Exactly 3-of-4 matching fields is not sufficient for a cache hit
Windows sharing a SnapshotCache instance do not bleed snapshots across policy or revision boundaries

command: cd ui && npm run test:run -- detachRestore
summary: 46 tests pass; all six session lifecycle properties (DR1–DR6) verified: detach/restore, close cancellation, subscription cleanup, focus return, heap recovery after 20 cycles, and no orphan listeners.

lifecycleProperties.name: Detach/Restore
lifecycleProperties.description: markDetached() transitions to 'detached' from all source states (idle, loading, ready, error, stale); validateDetachedRestore() returns true only when detached; reset() after detach returns to idle with generation=0 and revision=0.

lifecycleProperties.name: Close cancellation
lifecycleProperties.description: markDetached() aborts the active AbortController signal immediately; prior superseded signals are already aborted; calling markDetached() on idle (no controller) does not throw; reset() also aborts in-flight signals.

lifecycleProperties.name: Subscription cleanup
lifecycleProperties.description: After reset(): generation=0, revision=0, state='idle'. Stale generation tokens from before reset() are rejected by completeRequest/failRequest. guardRevision correctly rejects previously-set revisions after reset. Multiple resets are safe.

lifecycleProperties.name: Focus return
lifecycleProperties.description: failRequest() returns false and does not change state when generation doesn't match (stale response silently discarded). Also verified: stale completeRequest, failRequest on detached session, and that failRequest does not zero the revision.

lifecycleProperties.name: Heap recovery
lifecycleProperties.description: After 20 beginRequest+completeRequest cycles: state='ready', generation=20, revision=200. All 19 prior signals are aborted (no live orphan controllers). guardRevision reflects last revision only. reset() after 20 cycles returns clean state. 20 fail-only and 20 begin-only cycles also leave session consistent.

lifecycleProperties.name: No orphan listeners/workers
lifecycleProperties.description: With 2, 5, and 10 rapid beginRequest calls in sequence: only the last signal is alive; all prior signals are aborted. Each beginRequest returns a distinct AbortSignal instance. Generation increments monotonically. Two windows each issuing rapid requests do not share or cross-abort each other's controllers. After markDetached+reset, a fresh controller is created.

invariantsVerified: markDetached() always aborts the active AbortController and transitions to 'detached'
validateDetachedRestore() returns true iff state === 'detached'
reset() always brings generation, revision, and state back to initial values (0, 0, 'idle')
completeRequest/failRequest with mismatched generation are always no-ops (stale response safety)
Each beginRequest creates a new AbortController; the previous one is aborted immediately (no orphan)
After N request cycles, session holds only bounded scalar state — no accumulation of controllers, signals, or queries
AbortSignal instances are distinct objects per beginRequest call
